One product, many brands.

I work on a white-label platform for affiliate marketing that publishers and advertisers use across several brands. I own its React front end, its Elixir and Phoenix APIs, and the payment and data pipelines behind it.

I started in 2021 as a data analyst, writing Python to automate reports. In 2022 I moved into full-stack work and have stayed on the same codebase since, so I know where its sharp edges are.

I like problems where one change has to hold for every tenant: config, caching, auth, billing. Outside work I built tooldeck.co, a deals site for AI tools.

  1. Front end

    React front end for a multi-tenant platform

    Redux, Tailwind CSS and Material UI. One codebase serves several brands through per-domain white-label config.

  2. API

    REST APIs on Elixir and Phoenix

    PostgreSQL, token-based authentication, role-based access, and Redis caching for tenant config.

  3. Payments

    Payments and reconciliation pipeline

    Python and PostgreSQL, with ageing and settlement reports. It cut manual operational effort by 80%.

  4. Data

    Ingestion from partner APIs

    Elixir and Ruby pipelines pull multiple third-party APIs into one schema with idempotent, event-based updates. Runbooks make each new integration repeatable.

  5. Billing

    Onboarding and billing flows

    Sign-up, per-tenant email verification, Stripe and bank-transfer payments, and resource provisioning.

  6. Releases

    Production releases and upgrades

    Optimized front-end builds on Linux behind NGINX, Elasticsearch and Kibana for monitoring, Jest and Playwright tests, and a phased React 16 to 17 upgrade.
